name: What types of damage should be repaired before putting a home up for sale or rent?

mainEntity.name: What types of damage should be repaired before putting a home up for sale or rent?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common repairs before listing or leasing include fixing drywall holes, touching up or repainting scuffed interior walls, repairing damaged trim or baseboards, and replacing cracked floor tiles. Addressing small cosmetic flaws prevents home inspectors or prospective tenants from assuming the property has hidden maintenance issues. Owner Abraham Becerra handles these interior finish trades directly with his crew, which keeps turnover scopes cohesive. Addressing worn door hardware, loose molding, and patchy drywall early also ensures listing photography looks crisp and well-kept.
acceptedAnswer.description: Key repairs include fixing drywall gouges, repainting scuffed walls, repairing cracked tiles, and securing loose trim or baseboards to pass inspection and attract buyers.
